title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Assistant Management Accountant

Liverpool (Hybrid Working)

Salary: £35,000 + Study Support + Excellent Career Development

A growing and innovative organisation is seeking an ambitious Assistant Management Accountant to join its finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone early in their finance career who has gained exposure to management accounts and is looking to develop their technical skills within a supportive and forward-thinking environment.

Offering hybrid working, study support and genuine progression opportunities, this role would suit an individual keen to build a long-term career within finance.

The Role

Reporting to the Finance Manager, you will support the production of monthly management accounts and work closely with stakeholders across the business to provide meaningful financial information and analysis.

This is a developmental position that will provide exposure to budgeting, forecasting, month-end processes and commercial finance activities, making it an ideal next step for an aspiring management accountant.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist with the preparation of monthly management accounts.
- Prepare and post journals, accruals and prepayments.
- Complete balance sheet reconciliations and investigate variances.
- Support month-end close activities and reporting deadlines.
- Assist in the production of management information and financial reports.
- Analyse financial performance and provide commentary on key trends.
- Support budgeting and forecasting processes.
- Assist with cash flow reporting and monitoring.
- Provide support during year-end audit processes.
- Work with non-finance stakeholders across the business.
- Contribute to process improvements and finance projects.

About You
- Previous experience within a finance role.
- Exposure to management accounts preparation.
- AAT qualified, studying towards ACCA/CIMA, or looking to begin studies.
- Strong Excel and analytical skills.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
- A proactive attitude and genuine desire to progress within finance.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

What's on Offer
- Salary of £35,000
- Hybrid working model with 2 days per week in the office
- Full study support package
- Permanent position
- Excellent mentoring and professional development
- Opportunity to progress within a growing finance function
- Supportive and collaborative culture

Apply Now

This opportunity is ideal for an Assistant Accountant, Finance Assistant or Accounts Assistant who has been involved in management accounts and is looking to take the next step towards a successful career in management accounting. If you're ambitious, eager to learn and looking for a role that offers genuine progression, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Job Advert
Job Advert
X1 Sales and Lettings - Finance Account Manager

Are you ready to join an exciting, fast paced, multi award winning property management company as part of our Finance Team in Liverpool. This is an opportunity to learn and develop your understanding of the property industry whilst contributing to the continued business success and growth at X1.
Welcome to X1
X1 is a dynamic and highly successful property management company, established in Liverpool in 2011. Since then, we have experienced significant growth and now operate offices across Liverpool, Manchester, Leeds and Kent.
We pride ourselves on being a multi-award-winning company, delivering a high-quality rental experience while building strong, lasting relationships with both our tenants and landlords.
Our growth has continued throughout 2026, with the number of managed properties now exceeding 4,750. As the business continues to expand, our team is growing rapidly to support our ever-increasing portfolio and maintain the high standards that X1 is known for.

Our Values
Our values of Quality, Teamwork, Accountability, Flexibility, Compliance and Fun are at the heart of our culture and the way we do things and essential to our sustained success.

The Role
This role is ideal for an outgoing, personable and level-headed individual who is eager to develop their knowledge and experience within the UK lettings industry.

The successful candidate will be responsible for:
- Overseeing the allocation of rental income across a portfolio of properties within multiple X1 buildings.
- Working closely with the Lettings team to allocate all outstanding rental receipts and assist with the preparation of weekly rental debt reports.
- Processing daily payments to landlords in both the UK and overseas, while assisting with any queries relating to landlord statements.
- Ensuring payments for works orders are made promptly to suppliers, contractors, agents and other relevant third parties through the CRM system.
- Producing monthly performance reports for each site within the allocated portfolio, analysing key metrics including occupancy rates, average rental trends, fees generated and outstanding debt.
- Reviewing business operational accounts, identifying potential risks and recommending process improvements to increase efficiency and profitability.

What you will bring:
Ideally, the successful candidate will have:
- Strong Excel skills and confidence working with spreadsheets and data.
- A keen interest in mathematics, finance and portfolio analysis.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage workload effectively and use their own initiative.
- Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach to their work.
- A personable and approachable character, with the ability to build positive relationships with internal colleagues and external clients.
- A positive attitude, with a genuine willingness to learn and develop within the role.
- A professional attitude and high standards of personal presentation.

Department: Finance
Contract: Permanent
Hours: Monday - Thursday, 9.30am - 5.00pm; Friday, 9.30am - 4.30pm
Salary: Competitive Closing date: 24th October 2026
Benefits: 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays - An investment in your ongoing training and development

title: Receptionist/Admin
description: The post-holder is a Receptionist.(2 Posts available) shift patterns 07:45am - 13:45pm and 12:30pm - 18.30pm We are looking for a Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team at Eastview Surgery. This is an important front-line role where you will help patients access the right care while supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. We are looking for someone who is Friendly, approachable and professional Reliable, organised and able to manage competing priorities Confident communicating with patients and colleagues Comfortable using computers and learning new systems Able to work independently and as part of a team Committed to providing excellent patient service You will have experience using EMIS Web. What you will be doing Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries Welcoming patients at the reception desk Booking and managing appointments Completing a variety of administrative tasks Working closely with our clinical and administrative teams Handling confidential information professionally The role is busy and varied, so you will need excellent communication and organisational skills, good attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm under pressure. The role is essential to supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice and ensuring patients receive a helpful, efficient and respectful service. Main Duties and Responsibilities Reception and Front Desk Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, caring and professional manner. Check patients in for appointments and assist with general enquiries. Support the smooth flow of patients through the practice. Communicate with clinicians and other team members when required. Keep the reception area calm, tidy and organised. Respect patients privacy and maintain confidentiality at all times. Telephone Calls and Patient Enquiries Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and courteously. Book, amend and cancel appointments accurately using EMIS. Respond to general enquiries and direct patients to the appropriate service or member of staff. Follow practice procedures when receiving urgent or emergency calls and escalate concerns immediately where required. Take clear and accurate messages and pass them to the appropriate clinician or administrator promptly. Communicate sensitively with patients who may be worried, distressed or frustrated. Administrative and Computer-Based Duties Update patient contact details, appointment information and records accurately. Process online appointment requests, messages and administrative queries. Maintain accurate patient records, tasks and worklists on EMIS Web. Monitor emails, call queues and other practice communication systems. Support the smooth running of the days appointments and reception services. Complete general administrative duties, including printing letters, preparing lists and entering data. Follow practice procedures for filing, communication and information sharing. Teamwork and Communication Work closely with reception colleagues to maintain appropriate cover for the front desk and telephone lines. Communicate clearly and professionally with clinicians, administrators and management. Provide additional cover during colleagues annual leave or sickness where required. Attend team meetings, training sessions and practice updates. Contribute ideas that could improve patient services or working processes. Promote a positive, respectful and supportive working environment. Professional Conduct and Compliance Follow all practice policies and procedures, including those relating to confidentiality, safeguarding, information governance and data protection. Maintain a professional, respectful and positive approach. Report incidents, risks or concerns promptly to the Reception Lead or Practice Manager. Complete all required mandatory training. Keep knowledge of practice systems, policies and procedures up to date. Work within the responsibilities and boundaries of the role. Skills and Attributes Essential Excellent communication and telephone skills. A friendly, polite and approachable manner. Confidence using computers and learning new systems. Good organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. Ability to remain calm and professional in a busy environment. Strong attention to detail and accuracy. A reliable, flexible and supportive approach to teamwork. Understanding of the importance of patient confidentiality. Commitment to providing a high standard of patient service. Desirable Previous experience in a GP practice, healthcare setting or customer-facing role. Experience using EMIS Web or another clinical record system. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion The postholder must promote equality, diversity and inclusion and treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, fairness and respect. Health and Safety The postholder must take reasonable care of their own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by their work. Any hazards, incidents or concerns must be reported promptly in accordance with practice procedures. Confidentiality and Data Protection All patient, staff and practice information must be treated as confidential. The postholder must follow UK GDPR, data protection requirements, NHS information governance standards and practice policies. General Responsibilities The postholder will be expected to: Uphold the values and reputation of Eastview Surgery Follow all practice policies, procedures and applicable NHS requirements. Take responsibility for their own learning, training and professional development. Contribute to a positive, supportive and inclusive workplace. Carry out other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. This job description provides an overview of the role and is not exhaustive. Duties may change as the needs of the practice develop, following appropriate discussion with the postholder and their line manager.

title: Health Records Clerk
company: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
description: The Health Records Clerk is responsible for the accurate, complete and timely availability of patient records and documentation within the Electronic Document Management Systems as part of the patient clinical record. The role involves being responsible for document retrieval, preparation, scanning, indexing and quality assurance processes in line with departmental procedures including the use of the EDMS, PAS and EMIS systems, along with a number of other systems and IT processes. Working as a member of the Health Records Scanning Bureau, the post holder will be responsible for retrieval, transportation, archiving, preparation, indexing, scanning, sorting, handling and quality assurance of health records, supporting the digitisation of paper-based records into the Trust Electronic Document Management Systems (EDMS), Hyland Onbase and EMIS in line with departmental procedures. The role is vital to support service users regarding health records related processes including medical staff, nursing staff, allied health professionals, medical secretaries, administrators and external agencies. Document preparation and manual scanning includes frequently being seated whilst completing these tasks.All post holders are to be involved in and adaptable to future changes in the scope and location of their role, supporting health records processes and being receptive to change as the Trust EPR and EDMS solutions develop and mature over time, in particular supporting processes that are compliant with BS10008 scanning standards. Locate (using software such as CD View, Dip, Restore and PAS) request, obtain and make available case notes from main library and Off-Site Storage locations as required to be scanned into EDMS. Communicate with Apogee to arrange the return of critical care charts. Receive, sort and send internal/external post forwarding to relevant team/ward as appropriate. This includes returning, tracking and ensuring the delivery of case notes to other trusts via post. Liaise effectively with all disciplines of staff and other staff to ensure efficient lines of communication are maintained at all times. Answer the telephone and deal with queries and requests in a prompt, pleasant and helpful manner, referring on, as necessary to the appropriate Team. Participate and contribute to departmental meetings and feedback discussions. Minimize hazards and report any identifiable hazards to Line Manager. Adhere to all safe systems of work applicable to the work area. Report any information related incidents direct to the departmental manager immediately and ensure the Trust incident reporting process is followed. Follow Trust and departmental processes and procedures to ensure a high quality, resource efficient and cost-effective service is provided. Prepare documentation for scanning in line with departmental procedures, ensuring the records that are required are scanned into the EDMS, including utilisation of PAS to produce indexing barcodes. Scan documentation using the departmental scanning devices and index records accordingly to ensure documentation is classified and indexed to the correct patient record. Collect and transport paper records requiring scanning or archive from all areas of the organisation as required. Undertake photocopying, filing or other administrative tasks when required. Ensure that lifting and handling guidelines are adhered to and comply with all Health and Safety requirements. Carry out regular maintenance and cleansing of scanning devices to ensure devices are appropriately maintained and remain operational. Issues, faults or damages must be reported immediately. Use trolleys safely in all areas of the hospital for the daily collection and transportation of health records from Wards and other departments. Undertake any other duties required by manager appropriate to the Grade and relevant to the role, being flexible to the needs of the service to support effective delivery of service and support future changes of the health records service. Governance & Quality Maintain the health records department, documentation prepping and document sorting areas ensuring confidentiality, security, integrity and availability of health records at all times. Ensure all requests for disclosure of information are directed to the Information Governance Team. Ensure all movements of case notes are appropriately and accurately tracked on PAS. Achieve a high standard of data quality when entering data into PAS or other departmental data capture processes e.g. activity logs, quality assurance logs. Receive and sort loose paper filing in preparation to be filed within case notes or scanned into the EDMS, ensuring documentation is scanned to appropriate visit ID. Maintain accurate and up to date records of work completed daily to ensure departmental KPIs and service level agreements can be monitored. Undertake quality assurance processes to ensure documentation scanned into EDMS is indexed correctly and legible ensuring any deficiencies or issues are documented and rectified in a timely manner. Champion and comply with the Records Management, Information Governance and Data Quality Policies. Review the daily report from EDMS Scanning Tracking Location, and identify the correct process needed to ensure patients records are ordered/located. Ensure compliance with manual handling including health and safety requirements to maintain sufficient space within the health records department including archiving of records and boxes to off-site storage. Follow and comply with departmental procedure documentation. When new procedures are implemented or existing documentation updated, become familiar with the changes.

title: Medical Receptionist

EMIS Web system user for which experience is preferred but not essential as full training will be provided. We are a highly efficient and friendly team. Hours - Your hours will be 37.5 hours per week which will include reception, admin duties and a 30 minute paid lunch break each day. Salary - Your salary will be £12.71 per hour. There may also be overtime opportunities that arise. As a GP Practice Receptionist, you will be the first point of contact for patients, providing excellent customer service and administrative support to ensure the smooth running of the practice. The role requires someone with strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment Being the first point of contact for patients/visitors attending the practice. Greeting patients and handling telephone/email enquiries in a professional & friendly manner Booking, amending, and cancelling appointments using our clinical system Processing prescriptions and supporting clinicians with administrative tasks. Handling patient records, ensuring confidentiality and accuracy Previous experience in a GP surgery or healthcare environment (desirable but not essential) A GP receptionist serves as the first point of contact for patients. Providing administrative support, managing appointments and ensuring smooth practice operations whilst maintaining confidentiality and professionalism. Key responsibilities: Patient interactions and reception duties: Greeting patients and visitors in a professional and friendly manner both in person, via telephone and over email. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments using clinical systems. Assisting patients in accessing appropriate services or health care professionals efficiently. Acting as a chaperone during clinical examinations when required once adequate training is provided. Providing information about practice arrangements to prospective new or temporary patients. Administrative and clerical tasks: Processing repeat prescription requests and online consultation requests according to practice guidelines. Managing patient records which will involve coding and filing correspondence and medical notes. Supporting clinicians with administrative tasks. Maintaining the tidiness, safety and security of the practice premises. Attending staff meetings and undertaking training as required. Confidentiality and compliance: Handling sensitive patient information with strict confidentiality. Following practice policies and procedures and written protocols to ensure compliance with both practice and NHS standards. Reporting potential risks and supporting health, safety and infection control measures to senior members of staff.
